sources.entry: SSH Keys Manager - Native macOS app for managing local SSH keys and Git identities. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Stmol/ssh-keys-manager-macos-app) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS app (Swift/SwiftUI) for browsing, generating, organizing and copying local SSH keys and editing SSH config entries.
summary.what_it_does: Browses SSH keys in the default ~/.ssh directory or a custom directory and shows key metadata. Generates new key pairs with a chosen filename, key type, comment and optional passphrase, and can rename, duplicate, re-comment, change passphrases of, or remove keys. Creates, edits, reorders and deletes Host blocks in the SSH config through a form-based editor, and maps hosts to private keys via IdentityFile selection. The sidebar can check whether configured hosts are reachable directly. A menu bar interface lets you copy public and private keys without opening the main window. A Read-only mode blocks any operation that would modify existing SSH files.
use_cases: managing SSH keys on a Mac without the terminal
generating new SSH key pairs with a passphrase
copying public keys quickly from the menu bar
auditing an SSH setup safely in read-only mode
how_to_run: open "SSH Keys Manager.xcodeproj"  (then build and run the SSH Keys Manager scheme in Xcode)
make release-dmg VERSION=v0.1.0  (builds an unsigned release DMG locally)
make release-app VERSION=v0.1.0  (builds a local release .app)
notable: Read-only safety mode that blocks file-modifying operations
Menu bar access for copying public and private keys
Form-based SSH config Host block editor with IdentityFile mapping
Reachability check for configured SSH hosts from the sidebar
Make-based pipeline producing DMG and dSYM release assets
caveats: GitHub release builds are unsigned and not notarized, so macOS may report the app as damaged and require removing the quarantine attribute
Requires building from source with Xcode for the development route; the README does not describe other platforms
Parts of the codebase were AI-generated, which the README states was reviewed by a human developer
